# Detection rules

vigil ships 33 rules. Every alert carries the rule id, so an alert can be looked up here.

Severity decides who is woken up: each notifier has a `min_severity`, `high` by default.

## SSH access

### `ssh.key_added` {#ssh-key_added}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1098.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/004/)

**Alert:** `SSH key added to {file}: {comment}`

**Fires when:** A key appeared in a watched `authorized_keys` file.

**Known false positives:** Onboarding a teammate or a deploy key.

**What to do:** Check that someone on the team added it on purpose. A key added without a ticket is the most common way attackers keep access.

### `ssh.password_login` {#ssh-password_login}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1078](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/)

**Alert:** `Password login as {user} from {ip}`

**Fires when:** sshd accepted a password or keyboard-interactive login.

**Known false positives:** Hosts where password login is still intentionally enabled.

**What to do:** Confirm the person and the source address. If password login should be off, check `PasswordAuthentication` in sshd_config and rotate the password of that account.

### `ssh.unknown_key` {#ssh-unknown_key}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1098.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/004/)

**Alert:** `Login as {user} with a key not in authorized_keys ({fingerprint})`

**Fires when:** A public-key login used a key that is in none of the watched `authorized_keys` files.

**Known false positives:** `AuthorizedKeysCommand` or certificates, or an `authorized_keys` file outside the watch list.

**What to do:** Treat as compromise until explained: someone holds a key that the host does not list, or the key was added and removed between two scans.

### `ssh.new_source` {#ssh-new_source}

**Severity:** medium · **ATT&CK:** [T1078](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/)

**Alert:** `{user} logged in from new address {ip}`

**Fires when:** A user logged in over SSH from an address that user was never seen on before, on any host.

**Known false positives:** New home or mobile networks, travel, a teammate's first login. Every user raises it once per address.

**What to do:** Ask the user whether the login was theirs. Unexplained logins from new addresses are the classic sign of stolen credentials.

### `ssh.bruteforce` {#ssh-bruteforce}

**Severity:** low · **ATT&CK:** [T1110](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/)

**Alert:** `{count} failed SSH logins from {ip}`

**Fires when:** 30 or more failed SSH logins from one address within one batch interval.

**Known false positives:** Every server on the internet sees this. It is informational on its own.

**What to do:** Nothing, if password login is off. Correlate with a later `ssh.new_source` from the same address.

### `ssh.key_removed` {#ssh-key_removed}

**Severity:** low

**Alert:** `SSH key removed from {file}: {comment}`

**Fires when:** A key disappeared from a watched `authorized_keys` file.

**Known false positives:** Offboarding, key rotation.

**What to do:** None, unless nobody removed it; then someone may be cleaning up after themselves.

## Accounts

### `user.root` {#user-root}

**Severity:** critical · **ATT&CK:** [T1078.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/003/)

**Alert:** `Account {user} now has uid 0`

**Fires when:** An account other than root has uid 0, either new or changed to 0.

**Known false positives:** None known.

**What to do:** Treat as compromise. A second uid 0 account is a hidden root login.

### `user.added` {#user-added}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1136.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1136/001/)

**Alert:** `New account {user} (uid {uid})`

**Fires when:** A new account appeared in `/etc/passwd`.

**Known false positives:** Package installs that create system users (for example a new service).

**What to do:** Check which package or person created it. Interactive accounts that nobody remembers creating are a persistence mechanism.

### `user.removed` {#user-removed}

**Severity:** low · **ATT&CK:** [T1531](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1531/)

**Alert:** `Account {user} removed`

**Fires when:** An account disappeared from `/etc/passwd`.

**Known false positives:** Package removal, offboarding.

**What to do:** None, unless unexpected; removing accounts can also destroy evidence or lock admins out.

## Persistence and configuration files

### `file.preload` {#file-preload}

**Severity:** critical · **ATT&CK:** [T1574.006](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/006/)

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** `/etc/ld.so.preload` was created or changed.

**Known false positives:** Almost none. Very few legitimate setups use it.

**What to do:** Treat as compromise. Any library listed there is loaded into every process, a common userland rootkit technique.

### `file.cron` {#file-cron}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1053.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/003/)

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** A crontab or a file in a cron directory was added, changed or removed.

**Known false positives:** Admins adding jobs, packages installing cron entries.

**What to do:** Read the job. Cron entries that download or run something from `/tmp` or the network are persistence.

### `file.pam` {#file-pam}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1556.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1556/003/)

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** A PAM configuration file in `/etc/pam.d` changed.

**Known false positives:** Package updates that touch PAM.

**What to do:** Compare with the package version. A modified PAM stack can log passwords or accept any password.

### `file.sudo` {#file-sudo}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1548.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/003/)

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** `/etc/sudoers` or a file in `/etc/sudoers.d` changed.

**Known false positives:** Admin changes, package installs that add sudo rules.

**What to do:** Read the change. New `NOPASSWD` rules for unexpected users are privilege escalation paths.

### `file.accounts` {#file-accounts}

**Severity:** medium · **ATT&CK:** [T1098](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/)

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** `/etc/passwd`, `shadow`, `group` or `gshadow` changed without a specific account rule matching.

**Known false positives:** Password changes, group membership changes.

**What to do:** Check whether someone changed a password or added a user to a privileged group such as `sudo` or `docker`.

### `file.shell_init` {#file-shell_init}

**Severity:** medium · **ATT&CK:** [T1546.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/004/)

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** A shell startup file (`/etc/profile`, `profile.d`, bashrc, `rc.local`) changed.

**Known false positives:** Admin edits, packages adding environment setup.

**What to do:** Read the change. Code in shell init files runs at every login.

### `file.sshd` {#file-sshd}

**Severity:** medium · **ATT&CK:** [T1098](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/)

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** The SSH server configuration changed.

**Known false positives:** Hardening work, package updates.

**What to do:** Check what changed, especially `PermitRootLogin`, `PasswordAuthentication`, `AuthorizedKeysFile` and `AuthorizedKeysCommand`.

### `file.systemd` {#file-systemd}

**Severity:** medium · **ATT&CK:** [T1543.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/002/)

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** A unit file in `/etc/systemd/system` was added, changed or removed.

**Known false positives:** Every service install or `systemctl enable`.

**What to do:** Check that the unit belongs to something you installed. A new unit that runs a script from an odd place is persistence.

### `file.other` {#file-other}

**Severity:** low

**Alert:** `{path}: {change}`

**Fires when:** A file from `extra_watch` or another watched path changed.

**Known false positives:** Depends on what you added to the watch list.

**What to do:** Review the change.

## Exposure

### `port.docker` {#port-docker}

**Severity:** high

**Alert:** `Docker publishes {proto}/{port} on {addr}, past the host firewall`

**Fires when:** Docker published a container port on a non-loopback address. Docker writes NAT rules that are evaluated before the host firewall's input rules, so ufw and similar tools do not protect this port.

**Known false positives:** Containers that are meant to be public.

**What to do:** If the port should not be public, bind it to `127.0.0.1` in the compose file or filter it in the `DOCKER-USER` chain. Then accept the port in the dashboard.

### `port.public` {#port-public}

**Severity:** medium

**Alert:** `New port {proto}/{port} on {addr} ({process})`

**Fires when:** A new listening port appeared on a non-loopback address.

**Known false positives:** New services, programs that pick a random port on every start (game servers, Wine).

**What to do:** Check the process. Accept the port, or all ports of the process, in the dashboard if it is expected. An unknown process listening publicly can be a backdoor.

### `port.local` {#port-local}

**Severity:** low

**Alert:** `New local port {proto}/{port} ({process})`

**Fires when:** A new listening port appeared on loopback.

**Known false positives:** Local helper processes, debuggers, language servers.

**What to do:** Usually harmless; check the process name.

## Canaries

### `canary.opened` {#canary-opened}

**Severity:** critical · **ATT&CK:** [T1552.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/)

**Alert:** `Canary {path} opened by {exe} (uid {uid})`

**Fires when:** A process opened a canary file. Canaries are decoys that no legitimate workflow touches.

**Known false positives:** Backup tools, indexers, antivirus scans or an admin who forgot where the canaries are. Add tools to `canary_ignore_exe`.

**What to do:** Treat as an intrusion until explained. The alert names the process, user and parent chain; look for the SSH session behind it.

### `canary.tampered` {#canary-tampered}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1070.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/004/)

**Alert:** `Canary {path}: {problem}`

**Fires when:** A canary file was deleted, replaced or modified.

**Known false positives:** Cleanup scripts that delete old files in the canary's directory.

**What to do:** Someone found the canary. Check who was logged in at the time.

### `canary.overflow` {#canary-overflow}

**Severity:** medium

**Alert:** `Canary event queue overflowed on {host}`

**Fires when:** The kernel dropped canary events because they arrived faster than the agent could read them.

**Known false positives:** A tool that opens canaries in a tight loop.

**What to do:** Check what is reading the canaries; some opens were not attributed.

### `canary.remove_failed` {#canary-remove_failed}

**Severity:** medium

**Alert:** `Canary {path} could not be removed: {error}`

**Fires when:** The agent refused to delete a canary because the file is no longer the one it created.

**Known false positives:** None.

**What to do:** Inspect the file by hand before removing it.

## Integrity of vigil itself

### `chain.broken` {#chain-broken}

**Severity:** critical · **ATT&CK:** [T1565.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1565/001/)

**Alert:** `Event chain broken: {error}`

**Fires when:** Verification of the hash-chained event log failed.

**Known false positives:** Disk corruption.

**What to do:** Assume someone edited the log on the server. Compare with the daily chain anchors sent to your notifiers.

### `agent.config_rejected` {#agent-config_rejected}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/)

**Alert:** `Agent {host} rejected a configuration ({reason})`

**Fires when:** An agent rejected a configuration because its signature or content did not match.

**Known false positives:** None known.

**What to do:** Someone is tampering with the traffic between agent and server, or the server key changed.

### `agent.forged` {#agent-forged}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1557](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/)

**Alert:** `Request with invalid signature for agent {agent} from {ip}`

**Fires when:** The server received a batch for an agent with an invalid signature, or a replayed batch.

**Known false positives:** A host whose clock jumped backwards by more than the batch interval: sequence numbers are derived from the clock.

**What to do:** Someone is trying to inject events. Check the source address.

### `agent.restarted` {#agent-restarted}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1562.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/)

**Alert:** `Agent {host} restarted after {gap} without monitoring`

**Fires when:** An agent started again after it had run before. The alert states how long the host was unwatched.

**Known false positives:** Reboots and updates outside a maintenance window.

**What to do:** Review what happened on the host during the gap; SSH and sudo entries from the gap are reported after the restart, canary opens are not.

### `agent.silent` {#agent-silent}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1562.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/)

**Alert:** `Agent {host} silent`

**Fires when:** An agent sent nothing for longer than `deadman_seconds`.

**Known false positives:** Host reboots, network outages, the VPN going down.

**What to do:** Check whether the host is up. If it is and the agent is gone, someone may have stopped it.

### `agent.stopped` {#agent-stopped}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1562.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/)

**Alert:** `Agent {host} was stopped`

**Fires when:** An agent reported that it is shutting down.

**Known false positives:** Planned restarts and updates. Announce them with a maintenance window in the dashboard.

**What to do:** Check who stopped it if no maintenance was planned.

### `log.spoofed` {#log-spoofed}

**Severity:** high · **ATT&CK:** [T1070](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/)

**Alert:** `Fake {identifier} log entry written by {comm} (uid {uid})`

**Fires when:** A process other than sshd or sudo wrote a journal entry that claims to come from them.

**Known false positives:** None known. `logger -t sshd` in a test script would trigger it.

**What to do:** Someone is trying to plant fake log entries. Find the process named in the alert.

### `agent.dropped` {#agent-dropped}

**Severity:** low

**Alert:** `Agent {host} dropped {count} events`

**Fires when:** An agent lost events because its queue was full while the server was unreachable.

**Known false positives:** Long server outages.

**What to do:** Restore the connection; consider raising `max_queue`.
